name: tie-cantilever-split
reference: Benchmark F4's equivalence half: the cantilever of Benchmark B1 cut in two at mid-span and welded back together with contact.add. The oracle is not a published number but the single-Body model beside it: case cantilever-hex8-im is the same 1 m x 100 mm x 100 mm steel beam at the same 25 mm lattice with the same incompatible-modes element, and it measures a tip deflection of -0.19011253665073974 mm (0.96 % from the Timoshenko value -0.1919619 mm it is gated against). Splitting the Body puts a tie of 25 node pairs at x = 500 mm where the single model had one set of nodes; the elimination is exact for a matched pairing, so the tied model reproduces the single one to 1e-10 relative -- only the summation order differs -- and the root still carries the whole 1 kN.

checks.note: the tip deflection cantilever-hex8-im measures on the single Body, in mm, to every digit it has: welding the beam back together changes nothing but the summation order
A7: the clamp carries the load; the tie's internal force is not a reaction
the clamp carries the whole 1 kN
